THIS TURN: Play Tropical Island. Cast Birds of Paradise (G). Pass. We have no instant plays this round.

TARGET: Next turn: Swamp, then Grist (1BG from Tropical, Swamp and Birds), then Grist +1 for an Insect token. Our turn after: Forest, and hold U for Stormtamer. Turn 4: Lamia (5 mana); tutor Executioner's Capsule or Seal of Doom to the graveyard. Turn 5: Muldrotha (6 mana), recasting Grist, Capsule and Seal every turn. Missing pieces: Sol Ring or Arcane Signet (ramp), Gray Merchant or Syr Konrad (closers).

WIN PATH: Lock the board with recurring removal by turns 7–9, then Muldrotha beats plus Gray Merchant drains. The fastest opponent is P4 (combo turns 5–7), then P3 (Vito). We close well after them, so interact early.

THREATS & ANSWERS: 1) P4: Pitiless Plunderer, Ashnod's Altar, Grave Pact. Answer: Grist −2 (sac the Insect token). Bojuka Bog for a stocked P4 graveyard (Reanimate/Bloodghast). 2) P3: Vito, Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Skullclamp. Answer: Grist −2. 3) P2: Giada early. Answer: Grist −2 if nothing worse is out. Don't chump-block, and avoid needless creature deaths while Sephiroth or Blood Artist is out; each death drains us.

HOLD: Bojuka Bog until P4's graveyard has real targets. If no target by our turn 4, play it as a tapped land on a turn with spare mana. Once Muldrotha is out, keep U open for Stormtamer to protect her.

REPLAN IF: Birds dies (skip Grist, play lands, delay). A Plunderer or Altar loop piece lands early (prioritise Grist −2 on it). We draw Sol Ring or Signet (Muldrotha a turn sooner).

review.biggest_miss: The memo assigns Grist -2 as the answer to Skullclamp, Ashnod's Altar and Grave Pact. Grist -2 only destroys a creature or planeswalker. That leaves the key artifact and enchantment engines (Skullclamp, Altar, Grave Pact, Exquisite Blood, Sanguine Bond) with no planned answer. Lamia's tutor should fill that gap by binning Seal of Primordium or Assassin's Trophy-style removal, and the memo never notices this. It also miscounts land drops: holding Bojuka Bog breaks its own turn-4 Lamia and turn-5 Muldrotha curve.

shortcomings.what: It lists Grist -2 as the answer to non-creature threats (Skullclamp, Ashnod's Altar, Grave Pact). As a result, no answer is earmarked for artifact or enchantment engines, and Lamia's tutor target isn't chosen with them in mind (Seal of Primordium).

Mana curve error. We hold only 4 lands (Trop, Swamp, Forest, Bog). If Forest goes down on turn 3 and Bog is held, turn 4 has only 4 mana, not the 5 Lamia needs. Bog should be played tapped on turn 3, which costs nothing, with Forest on turn 4. Muldrotha on turn 5 also needs one more land drawn, and the memo doesn't flag this.

It gives no warning about wipe exposure or about staying lean. Birds is our only ramp and Grist is our only removal. P2 actually runs Wrath of God, Austere Command and Farewell (which can exile our graveyard). P3 runs Damn and Olivia's Wrath. The dossiers only hinted at this.
shortcomings.missing_info: P2's actual wipe suite (Farewell, Wrath, Austere Command) and P3's (Damn, Olivia's Wrath)

shortcomings.what: It doesn't name P3's real enchantment combo (Exquisite Blood plus Sanguine Bond, not only Vito) or Viscera Seer. These need enchantment answers, and Grist can't provide one.
shortcomings.missing_info: P3 runs Sanguine Bond + Exquisite Blood and Viscera Seer

shortcomings.what: It doesn't note that Giada is P2's cheap commander and likely lands next turn. It doesn't weigh an early Grist -2 on Giada, which slows the whole Angel chain, against saving Grist loyalty.

It says 'avoid creature deaths' but still plans Grist -2 by sacrificing the Insect. It never notes that the sacrifice feeds Sephiroth's or Blood Artist's drains and counts toward Sephiroth's transform. Grist should also +1 on turn 2 to reach 4 loyalty before any -2.

errors: Grist -2 cannot destroy Skullclamp, Ashnod's Altar or Grave Pact. It hits only creatures and planeswalkers.
The 'Turn 4: Lamia (5 mana)' plan is impossible with our lands if Bog is held and Forest goes down on turn 3. Only 4 mana would be available.
Turn numbering is inconsistent: 'Turn 4/Turn 5' is mixed with 'next turn/our turn after'.

WIN PATH: Stabilise, then drain P2 (at 11) with repeated Gray Merchants plus Lamia combat. It's slow; P1 can kill us in about 3-4 turns from 34.

THREATS & ANSWERS:
1) P1: The Scarab God and Teval. Use Hostage Taker on Scarab God (exile, and we can cast it). Fel's -3 or Plaguecrafter for Teval. Lamia blocks Scarab God.
2) P3's Archangel of Tithes: Fel's -3.
3) P2's Hearthhull if cast: Assassin's Trophy.
Keep Lamia home as a blocker.

review.biggest_miss: The memo plans against a board that will not exist. Planetary Annihilation also deals 6 damage to each creature, so Teval, Scarab God, Hedron Crab, the Zombie, the countered River Kelpie and Archangel of Tithes all die. Only the damage clause was an information gap (the text was truncated). The real new threat was visible in the given card text, and that part is a reasoning failure: The Scarab God dies, returns to P1's hand at the next end step, gets recast, and can pay {2}{U}{B} to exile Muldrotha from our graveyard. That turns our lynchpin into P1's 4/4 Muldrotha. Getting Muldrotha out of the graveyard fast (Animate Dead, Eternal Witness, Demonic Tutor, or Survival of the Fittest into Witness) is the whole turn. The memo also leaned on graveyard cards (Assassin's Trophy, Fel, Plaguecrafter) as answers even though they are unusable until Muldrotha is back.

shortcomings.what: Did not realise Planetary Annihilation also deals 6 damage to each creature. The threat list (Scarab God, Teval, Archangel), 'Lamia blocks Scarab God' and 'Fel -3 on Archangel' are all moot after it resolves.
shortcomings.missing_info: Full oracle text of Planetary Annihilation (the stack entry was truncated; it deals 6 damage to each creature)

shortcomings.what: Missed that The Scarab God (text provided) returns to P1's hand and can later exile Muldrotha from our graveyard to make a token copy for P1. This is the urgent reason to get Muldrotha out of the yard.

Listed Assassin's Trophy as the answer to Hearthhull. It is an instant in our graveyard, and Muldrotha only casts permanent spells. Fel, Plaguecrafter and Hostage Taker were also listed without noting they need Muldrotha on board.
Missed the Survival of the Fittest out: discard Gary, fetch Eternal Witness, return Muldrotha, 5 mana total. Also gave no plan for drawing a land (8 mana).

Gave no wipe or removal exposure warning. Muldrotha returned by Animate Dead dies to any enchantment removal, and a single wipe from P3 (Wrath/Farewell) or P2 (Blasphemous Act) undoes the rebuild. The memo also did not note that the annihilation turns off P1's Field of the Dead (6 lands) while stocking P1's graveyard with 9+ lands and its dead creatures for Living Death or Reanimate.
The closing engine is vague. Gary needs a sacrifice outlet to recur each turn. Lamia's search should set that up (Claws of Gix in the artifact lane), not fetch Massacre Wurm onto an empty board.

errors: Assassin's Trophy is in the graveyard. It is an instant, so it cannot be cast through Muldrotha, and Muldrotha is not even on the battlefield.
It assumes Scarab God, Teval and Archangel of Tithes survive; all take 6 damage and die (info gap).
'P1 can kill us in 3-4 turns' is unsupported, especially after a creature wipe.
It counts 7 mana without accounting for a possible land drop (8).

results.memo:
THIS TURN: 1) Tap all 8 (Sol Ring plus six lands) and cast Muldrotha, using B, G and U from Overgrown Tomb, Forest and Breeding Pool. 2) If Muldrotha resolves, play Misty Rainforest from the graveyard as the land drop. Crack it for Underground Sea (untapped) and keep that U open for Stormtamer. If Muldrotha is countered, play Tropical Island instead. 3) Attack P1 with Siren Stormtamer. P1 has no flyers or reach, so we take the monarchy and switch off Regal Behemoth's mana doubling. Stormtamer can still be sacrificed while tapped. 4) Draw from the monarch at end step.

TARGET: Next turn has 11 mana (Tropical Island is the land drop):
- Baleful Strix, artifact lane, 2
- Grist, planeswalker lane, 3: −2, sacrificing Strix, to destroy Gitrog
- Gwen Stacy, enchantment lane, 3: destroy Teval
- Shriekmaw evoke, creature lane, 2: kill Behemoth, or Pantlaza if it's out
- Keep 1 U up for Stormtamer.

WIN PATH: After the board is clean, cast Syr Konrad. Each Shriekmaw or Mulldrifter evoke then pings every opponent twice (once on death, once when it leaves the graveyard). Add Braids for a 2-point drain each end step. Tutor for Gray Merchant later. That's roughly 6–8 turns, and all three opponents are live.

THREATS & ANSWERS:
1) P3: Sauron grows the deathtouch Army with every spell we cast. Answer it with a Braids edict, or Toxic Deluge via Demonic Tutor later. Vraska −3 can kill Dreadhorde Invasion. Cast few spells.
2) P1: Behemoth, the monarchy and Pantlaza. Shriekmaw handles these; Teval, Gitrog and Sauron are black, so Shriekmaw can't hit them.
3) P4: Gitrog goes to Grist, Teval to Gwen Stacy.

HOLD: Stormtamer plus U for removal aimed at Muldrotha. Keep Braids, Konrad and Mind Stone in hand, since every extra spell grows the Army.

REPLAN IF: Muldrotha dies or is countered. Pantlaza lands. We get a wipe or graveyard hate. We lose the monarchy.

review.biggest_miss: The memo ranks P3's Sauron as the top threat, then plans five spells over two turns (Muldrotha plus four lane casts). Each one amasses P3's deathtouch Army, and P3 has 0 cards in hand, so every Army hit is a free draw-4 wheel. The only answer it names for Sauron is a 'Braids edict'. Braids is not an edict: each opponent chooses whether to sacrifice, and which permanent. It never considers actually killing Sauron. It could: Grist −2 (sacrificing Strix) targeting Sauron, paying ward by sacrificing Braids from hand. Braids and Strix then come back through the creature and artifact lanes. The two cards it does earmark go to lower-value jobs: Gwen Stacy on Teval, which the dossier says doesn't stop P4's engine, and Shriekmaw on a Behemoth that is harmless once we hold the monarchy.

shortcomings.what: Gives no real answer to Sauron's engine, which grows off every spell we cast and wheels P3 from an empty hand. It wrongly treats Braids as a forced edict and misses the Grist −2 line that pays ward with a recursive legendary (Braids).
Overcounts next turn's mana. 6 lands + Sol Ring (8), + fetched Underground Sea, + Tropical Island = 10, not 11. The listed plan (2+3+3+2+1 U) needs 11, so the executor cannot run it.

Gwen Stacy chapter I on Teval is low value. Teval returns from the command zone, and per the dossier its engine runs without it. Gwen's better uses are Gitrog or the Army. Chapter III can also exile P3's and P4's graveyards before Living Death, and the memo doesn't mention that.
Spends Shriekmaw on Regal Behemoth after the Stormtamer attack has already taken the monarchy away. It should be held for Pantlaza or Wrathful Raptors.

Taking the monarchy makes us the target of a deathtouch Army, Gitrog and flying Teval. The memo doesn't warn against blocking deathtouch with Muldrotha, and doesn't suggest recurring Baleful Strix as a deathtouch flying blocker.

Doesn't point out that this turn is a safe window: P1 and P3 are fully tapped (only Barad-dûr up, no hand), and P4 has 1 land open. It also doesn't tell the executor which removal Stormtamer must save its sacrifice for on opponents' turns.
Misses the pilot note that Grist can go through the creature lane, which frees the planeswalker lane for Vraska (−3 can kill the MV-0 Army token or Dreadhorde Invasion).
The win path (Konrad pings, 6–8 turns) is never compared to the opponents' clocks. Recurring Massacre Wurm and Gray Merchant are left vague.

Wipe exposure for Muldrotha was underweighted. P1 actually runs Blasphemous Act, Swords, Path and Generous Gift, and P3 runs Toxic Deluge. The P1 dossier only mentioned Path and Wakening Sun's Avatar.
shortcomings.missing_info: P1's full removal and wipe suite (Blasphemous Act, Swords to Plowshares, Generous Gift) and P3's Toxic Deluge

errors: Says next turn has 11 mana; it is 10 (6 lands + Sol Ring, + Underground Sea, + Tropical Island).
Calls Braids an edict answer to Sauron. Braids lets each opponent choose whether to sacrifice and which permanent to sacrifice, and a player who declines loses 2 life and we draw.
The next-turn plan costs 11 and cannot be executed with the mana available.

If Muldrotha is countered, play Tropical Island instead. 3) Attack P1 with Stormtamer (no flyers or reach). We become monarch and switch off Behemoth's extra mana. Stormtamer can be sacrificed while tapped. 4) Monarch draw at end step.
ON THEIR TURNS: Sacrifice Stormtamer only to save Muldrotha (Putrefy, Trophy, Tear Asunder, Swords, Path). Never block the deathtouch Army or Gitrog with Muldrotha. We're at 35, so take the hit.
NEXT TURN (10 mana; land drop is Misty from the graveyard again or Tropical): Braids from hand (3), Baleful Strix in the artifact lane (2, draw), Grist in the planeswalker lane (3), then Grist −2 sacrificing Strix, targeting SAURON. Pay ward by sacrificing Braids. Sauron dies, which stops the Army growth and the wheel. 2 mana left: keep U for Stormtamer. Following turn: Braids and Strix come back through their lanes, and Gwen Stacy (enchantment lane) goes on Gitrog. Chapter III exiles P3's and P4's yards before Living Death.
THREATS: 1) P3: Sauron plus a deathtouch Army that grows with each of our spells. Hand 0, so each Army hit is a free draw 4. Kill Sauron first. Vraska −3 can kill the Army token or Dreadhorde Invasion later. 2) P4: Gitrog (Gwen or Grist), holding removal and Living Death. 3) P1: once the monarchy is gone, Behemoth is just a 5/5. Save Shriekmaw for Pantlaza or Wrathful Raptors.

We aim to close about 4 turns after the lock. The opponents need about 3–5 more turns, so stay ahead by killing their engines, not their bodies.
HOLD: Konrad and Mind Stone until Sauron is gone. Expect Blasphemous Act or Toxic Deluge, so don't flood the board.
REPLAN IF: Muldrotha dies, Pantlaza lands, Living Death is cast, or Sauron is recast.

results.memo:

1) Cast Braids, Arisen Nightmare (all 3 mana).
2) At our end step, have Braids sacrifice Cryogen Relic. The Relic draws 1 as it leaves. P2 and P4 have no artifacts, so each loses 2 and we draw 2 more. P3 either sacrifices The Masamune or loses 2 and we draw.
3) At cleanup, discard down to 7. Discard permanents, not lands or Swan Song, since Muldrotha can replay them later.
No blocks with Braids against first-strike vampires, and never chump.

TARGET: Next turn, play a land, cast Talisman of Dominance, then Grist (+1 for an Insect token) or Barrin. The turn after, cast Muldrotha with 5 lands plus Talisman. Then recast Plaguecrafter, fetches and Relic from the graveyard. Tutor targets: Pernicious Deed, Claws of Gix, Gray Merchant.

WIN PATH: Braids drains about 4 per turn cycle and draws. After Muldrotha, add Gray Merchant and Syr Konrad. Aim to win by round 10. P2's poison and P3's loop threaten rounds 7–9.

THREATS & ANSWERS:
1) P2's Plague Stinger (poison clock): Grist -2 (sacrifice the Insect token) or Barrin bounce.
2) P3's Sephiroth plus any outlet: Grist, or Plaguecrafter later.
3) P4's Captain and Shared Animosity (about 6 damage a turn): Seal of Primordium on Animosity only if nothing worse appears. Save Seal first for Exquisite Blood, Skullclamp, Grave Pact or Ashnod's Altar.

HOLD: Seal of Primordium, Swan Song (keep U open once we have spare mana), Ratchet Bomb (tick it toward 3 later, not now), Glen Elendra until we have 4 spare mana.

REPLAN IF: Braids is removed (next turn, cast Talisman plus Grist), Atraxa or Vito lands, or P2 reaches 5+ poison on anyone.

review.biggest_miss: The memo ignored The Masamune, even though its text was given. Once it is equipped to Sephiroth, every creature death triggers Sephiroth twice, so it transforms after only two deaths. Its 'must be blocked if able' clause also means that if P3 equips it ({2}) and swings at us, Braids is forced to block, dies to first strike, and feeds two drains. The memo's 'never chump' instruction cannot be followed in that case. The memo also spends Grist's -2 on a 1/1 Plague Stinger when it should be earmarked for Atraxa. P2 has six lands and Atraxa is uncast.

shortcomings.what: The Masamune is not treated as a threat. It doubles Sephiroth's death triggers, which halves the four-death transform threshold. It also forces Braids to block, so the memo's 'never block/chump' instruction is unenforceable if P3 equips and attacks us. Seal of Primordium on Masamune should be at least considered.

Grist's -2 is earmarked for Plague Stinger, a 1/1 slow poison clock. It should be held for Atraxa, since P2 has six lands and the commander in the command zone, or for Tekuthal/Vorinclex or a Sephiroth about to transform. Stinger can later be blocked by Glen Elendra (flying) or answered by a recurring Relic stun.

Swan Song is framed only as Muldrotha protection. It is also our best answer to the enchantment win pieces: Exquisite Blood, Grave Pact, Inexorable Tide, Doubling Season, Prologue to Phyresis. It also stops sorcery wipes such as Damn and Olivia's Wrath.

P4 runs Exquisite Blood plus Sanguine Bond, a second two-card infinite beyond the Vito line in the dossier. It also runs Damn, Olivia's Wrath and Teferi's Protection. This raises the value of holding Seal of Primordium and Swan Song for enchantments and makes wipes risky to rely on.
shortcomings.missing_info: P4's actual list: Sanguine Bond, Damn and Teferi's Protection alongside Exquisite Blood

shortcomings.what: P2 runs Doubling Season and Contagion Engine, which accelerate proliferate. Doubling Season would be a Swan Song target and Contagion Engine a Seal target.
shortcomings.missing_info: P2's actual list (Doubling Season, Contagion Engine, Norn's Decree)

shortcomings.what: The win path is vague. Braids alone deals about 4–6 per round against 117 combined life. The memo misses the real engine: Muldrotha recasts Cryogen Relic from the artifact lane each turn and Braids sacrifices it at end step, for about three cards plus a drain every turn. It also never compares our clock with P3's turn 5–7 loop, which is now live, or with P4's Vito and Blood combos.

The memo does not flag that P4's single open land, Path of Ancestry, is exactly Swords to Plowshares or Path to Exile mana for Braids. It also leaves out Ratchet Bomb's self-hit at 3, which would kill our own Braids, Barrin and Grist along with Sephiroth, Masamune, Captain and Animosity.

errors: The discard rationale is muddled: 'discard permanents, not lands... since Muldrotha can replay them.' Muldrotha replays lands too. Keep lands because we are land-short (3 lands, turn ~6), not because they can't be recurred.
The memo also never says how many cards will be discarded: roughly 3–4 after drawing 3–4 at end step. Priority guidance was needed.
Using Grist -2 on Plague Stinger is a poor use of a planeswalker ability while an uncast Atraxa looms. This is a misallocation rather than a rules error.

2) End step: Braids sacrifices Cryogen Relic. The Relic draws 1. P2 and P4 have no artifacts, so each loses 2 and we draw 2. P3 either sacrifices The Masamune, which is great, or loses 2 and we draw.

ANSWERS:

- Seal of Primordium: Exquisite Blood, Skullclamp, Grave Pact or Ashnod's Altar. Hit The Masamune if P3 starts making fodder.

shortcomings.what: Toxic Deluge is set at X=5, which kills everything except the one card the plan is built around. X=10 is needed, and it requires more than 10 life. There is no guidance on keeping our life above that.

The clock is misjudged. P2 is in main phase 1 with 22 flying/vigilance power (Avacyn 11, Lyra 5, Giada 3, three 1/1 tokens) and will attack now. Our next turn is realistically the only turn to answer Avacyn.

Library outs that fit our mana are missing. Demonic Tutor (2) into Deluge (3) or Invasion (4). Survival of the Fittest (2), discarding Vrock, into Hostage Taker (4). Hostage Taker (4) plus Plaguecrafter (3) on 7 mana. Otawara channel at instant speed as a tempo bounce.

Animate Dead is named only as a way back for Muldrotha. The payoff is missed: Muldrotha lets us recast Spore Frog from the graveyard as a recurring Fog, plus Kaya's Ghostform on Muldrotha. That is the actual survival engine.

Hostage Taker is fragile against this opponent. P2 runs Path, Swords, Generous Gift and Stroke of Midnight, and removing Taker returns Avacyn. Invasion or Deluge are permanent answers and should be preferred.

review.biggest_miss: The memo treats Massacre Wurm as a free swing, but the Wurm has serious costs. Its six deaths trigger P4's Blood Artist and P3's Sephiroth once each, so up to about 12 life drains at us. That takes us from 24 to roughly 12, which is the memo's own replan line, and leaves P4's roughly 50-power board needing far less to kill us. The deaths also transform Sephiroth into a permanent drain emblem and hand P3 6 Treasures (Pitiless Plunderer) and 4 Spawns (Pawn of Ulamog). Worse, the untapped Gray Merchant on P4's board is our own card: it was cast last turn per the previous memo and then stolen by Captivating Vampire. The Wurm is the next likely steal target. Once P4 controls it, its static costs us 2 per creature death, and P4 gains a pumped 6/5 Vampire. The -2/-2 kills nothing of P4's, because every P4 creature has 4 or more toughness. The Wurm is still the only play, but the memo should have priced these costs and planned for the steal.

shortcomings.what: Did not count the drain backlash from six deaths: 6 from P4's Blood Artist plus 6 from P3's Sephiroth, which could put us near 12 life. It also ignored that P3 gains 6, so P3's net loss is 6, not 12.

Missed that the Gray Merchant on P4's board was stolen from us by Captivating Vampire, so a Wurm steal on P4's turn is the expected line, not a side note. With the Wurm stolen, the Elder chump costs us 2 extra life.

Did not weigh what P3 gains from the sweep: a permanent Sephiroth emblem, 6 Treasures, 4 Spawns and a Morbid Opportunist card. The dossier says to kill Sephiroth before four deaths; the memo just labels the transform an 'accepted cost'.

The recovery math is wrong. Demonic Tutor into Eternal Witness into Muldrotha costs 11 mana, and we will have 9. Demonic Tutor into Animate Dead costs 4 and leaves mana to recast Claws, Ratchet Bomb and Wayfarer's Bauble in the same turn.
Did not note that Toxic Deluge is a sorcery, which Muldrotha cannot recast. It is dead in the graveyard except through Eternal Witness, so our only real wipe answer to P4's board is out of reach.

Could not size P2's poison threat or P4's instant-speed interaction. P2's list includes Contagion Engine, Drown in Ichor, Norn's Decree and Infectious Bite. P4's list includes Teferi's Protection, Olivia's Wrath, Damn and Boros Charm. Atraxa's commander tax, which sets how soon she comes back, was also unknown.

2) P1 Pantlaza, Rhythm of the Wild or Wrathful Raptors: Capsule for nonblack creatures, Boseiju channel for Rhythm.

review.biggest_miss: The main line cannot be executed. Otawara taps only for blue. That leaves two green sources (Forest and Zagoth Triome), but Eternal Witness ({1}{G}{G}) plus Nature's Lore ({1}{G}) needs three green. After Witness resolves, Nature's Lore cannot be cast, which loses the Bayou and the extra mana for next turn. The land drop has to be Boseiju, which taps for G, with Otawara held for its channel. Otawara's bounce is also the better card to hold, since it answers The One Ring, Call of the Ring, Rhythm and Teval's Judgment.

shortcomings.what: Colored-mana sequencing error. Otawara as the land drop leaves only 2 green sources for 3 green pips, so Nature's Lore is uncastable after Eternal Witness.

Assigned Sinister Concoction as the answer to Sauron. Concoction targets, so Sauron's ward (sacrifice a legendary artifact or creature, which for us means Muldrotha) makes it a non-answer. The real answers are an edict (Plaguecrafter) or a wipe (Toxic Deluge, Pernicious Deed), all in the library.

Chose to hold Concoction and cast Capsule. Concoction hits any creature, including the black threats that Capsule misses (Sauron, Teval, the Army), and fires for only {B}. With it on board, next turn could be Muldrotha plus a live removal activation. Nothing is gained by holding it in hand.

Missed the channel-then-replay synergy. With Muldrotha out, a channeled Boseiju or Otawara goes to the graveyard and can come back as the land drop. Missed that Witness becomes a repeatable regrowth engine through the creature lane plus Claws of Gix.

No plan for Muldrotha meeting a counterspell next turn. The dossier already flagged Arcane Denial and Saruman's Trickery. P3 also runs Counterspell, Swan Song and An Offer You Can't Refuse. P4 runs Counterspell and An Offer You Can't Refuse.
